blocks.text: What this usually means in UK cars

ordered.title: The crucial distinction: condensation vs. coolant
ordered.description: White smoke from your exhaust is one of the most misunderstood symptoms. Here's the truth:

blocks.text: White vapour that disappears as the engine warms up. Every car does this in UK damp weather.
If smoke continues after the engine reaches operating temperature, coolant is entering the combustion chamber.

In our 24,650 quote dataset, 68% of persistent white smoke cases were caused by head gasket failure. The remaining 32% were cracked cylinder heads, intake manifold leaks, or EGR cooler failure (on diesels).
The crucial test: Does the smoke have a sweet smell? That's coolant burning. Head gasket failure is almost certain.

ordered.title: The expensive mistake is assuming it's harmless

cards.text: “It's just steam from the cold weather.” Condensation disappears when warm. If it persists, it's coolant burning.
cards.fullText: “It's just steam from the cold weather.” Condensation disappears when warm. If it persists, it's coolant burning.

cards.text: “I'll just top up the coolant and keep driving.” You're masking a serious problem. Coolant loss will lead to overheating and engine seizure.

blocks.text: Warning: These symptoms mean coolant is entering the combustion chamber. Continuing to drive will cause overheating, warped heads, and a seized engine.

ordered.title: The cost escalation with every stage

rows: Coolant and oil mix, engine damage

blocks.text: The Cost Escalation: A £550-£2,000 head gasket repair becomes a £2,500-£10,000+ engine replacement if ignored.

ordered.title: Three steps to protect your engine

items: Step 1: Check Your Coolant Level (£0) Check when engine is cold. Is the coolant level low? Is there oil in the coolant (mayonnaise-like sludge)?
Step 2: Check Your Oil (£0) Remove the dipstick or oil filler cap. Is there a creamy/milky substance? (coolant in oil). This confirms head gasket failure.

Step 3: Book Professional Diagnostic (£50-£150) A technician will perform a compression test, check for exhaust gases in coolant (chemical test), pressure test the cooling system, and inspect for external leaks.

ordered.title: Use vehicle value to avoid overspending
ordered.description: “If your vehicle is worth less than £2,000-£3,000 and head gasket has failed, consider scrapping rather than repairing.”

rows: Consider repair if vehicle otherwise good.
Repair properly; consider cylinder head replacement if damaged.

ordered.title: Common affected engines and root causes

items: VAG 1.8T/2.0T petrol: Head gasket failure common at 80,000-120,000 miles.
BMW N47 diesel: EGR cooler failure can cause white smoke - cheaper than head gasket.
Ford 1.0/1.6 EcoBoost: Known head gasket issues in early models.
Subaru flat-four engines: Head gasket failure is a known weakness - repair costs often higher due to engine layout.

blocks.text: Always verify the cause before booking head gasket work. EGR cooler failure on diesels looks identical but costs £200-£500 to fix.

blocks.question: How do I know if white smoke is condensation or head gasket? +
blocks.answer: Condensation disappears when the engine is warm. Head gasket smoke persists and has a sweet smell.

blocks.question: Can I drive with white smoke? +
blocks.answer: If it's condensation only - yes. If it's persistent, sweet-smelling, or comes with a warning light - no.

blocks.question: How much does head gasket repair cost in the UK? +
blocks.answer: Head gasket repair costs £550-£2,000+ depending on engine type, vehicle access, and whether the head needs skimming.

blocks.question: Is white smoke from a diesel different from petrol? +
blocks.answer: Diesel produces more condensation and can produce white smoke on cold start that looks like a problem - but if it persists, same rule applies.
